brihadeeswarar_temple.name: Brihadeeswarar Temple
brihadeeswarar_temple.short_description: A magnificent Shiva temple built by Raja Raja Chola I, famous for its towering vimana and the fact that its shadow never falls on the ground at noon.
interesting_facts: The Kumbam (apex stone) weighs 80 tonnes and was carved from a single rock
It is one of the few temples where the shadow of the main tower does not fall on the ground at noon
Built entirely without the use of any binding material—stones were interlocked

hampi_virupaksha.name: Virupaksha Temple
hampi_virupaksha.unesco_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Group of Monuments at Hampi)
hampi_virupaksha.short_description: The oldest functioning temple in India, dedicated to Lord Shiva, located on the banks of the Tungabhadra River.
interesting_facts: It has been continuously worshipped for over 1,300 years
The temple's main tower is 160 feet tall
It survived the destruction of Hampi by Mughal forces in 1565 CE

konark_sun_temple.name: Konark Sun Temple
konark_sun_temple.short_description: A massive temple designed as a giant chariot of the Sun God, with intricately carved stone wheels, horses, and mythological figures.
interesting_facts: The temple is shaped like a chariot with 24 exquisitely carved wheels
Each wheel is a sundial that can accurately tell time
The main sanctum was originally 229 feet tall but collapsed

mahabalipuram_shore_temple.name: Shore Temple
mahabalipuram_shore_temple.unesco_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram)
mahabalipuram_shore_temple.short_description: A structural temple built on the shores of the Bay of Bengal, made of granite blocks, symbolizing the Pallava dynasty's architectural brilliance.
interesting_facts: It is one of the oldest structural (not rock-cut) temples in South India
It has survived centuries of sea erosion and cyclones
It served as a lighthouse for sailors in ancient times

qutub_minar.name: Qutub Minar
qutub_minar.short_description: A 73-meter tall victory tower, the tallest brick minaret in the world, marking the beginning of Indo-Islamic architecture in India.
interesting_facts: It has 379 steps and is 72.5 meters tall
The first three stories are made of red sandstone, the fourth and fifth of marble
It survived multiple earthquakes and was repaired several times
